items.title: Roy Palmer Interview, 1955-09-22
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...oh, Jasper Taylor. Yeah, Jasper Taylor, yeah. He was with him. He was with him. [INTERVIEWEE] Nice.

ctx.x: Yeah, he took a couple of lessons. He didn't stay, but he took enough to learn to play pretty good. He plays pretty good.

What's one of them? He's around. He, uh, up in our place where a friend, we have a piano, sort of a studio, not a real big recording studio, but some bands used to come up and rehearse. And about a year ago, he was there with a few people. Oh, yeah? I can't remember who, oh, Jasper Taylor. Yeah, Jasper Taylor, yeah. He was with him. He was with him.

items.title: Jasper Taylor Interview, 1959-06-30
items.q: he was, did all the trombone work for the, for the Handis Syndicate, and we had another one in the Syndicate.

ctx.x: Like Roy Palmer said he inspired him.

He was a great trombonist, and he was, did all the trombone work for the, for the Handis Syndicate, and we had another one in the Syndicate. His name was Higgins, the banjo. He played banjo and sang, and then we, another New Orleans man we had was Walls, the great bass player.
